preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 100000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]) and all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 100000 and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 100000 and int(line.split()[0]) != int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Input must contain valid integers for n (number of cities) and m (number of roads), where 2 ≤ n ≤ 100000 and 1 ≤ m ≤ 100000. Each road must connect two distinct cities, and city indices must be between 1 and n.
The input must have exactly m + 1 lines: one for n and m, and m lines for roads.

postconditions.description: The output must be a single integer representing the minimum number of separate cities after orienting all roads unidirectionally, where 0 ≤ output ≤ n.
The output is the minimum possible number of cities with no incoming roads after optimally orienting all roads unidirectionally.

candidate_issues.task_evidence: Help the Ministry of Transport to find the minimum possible number of separate cities after the reform.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition expression that ensures the output is the minimum possible number of cities with no incoming roads after optimally orienting all roads unidirectionally, derived from the input graph structure.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: The President of Berland decided to make changes to the road system and instructed the Ministry of Transport to make this reform. Now, each road should be unidirectional (only lead from one city to another). In order not to cause great resentment among residents, the reform needs to be conducted so that there can be as few separate cities as possible. A city is considered separate, if no road leads into it, while it is allowed to have roads leading from this city.
